source.text: וַיְהִ֡י בִּימֵ֣י אָ֠חָז בֶּן־יוֹתָ֨ם בֶּן־עֻזִּיָּ֜הוּ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֗ה עָלָ֣ה רְצִ֣ין מֶֽלֶךְ־אֲ֠רָם וּפֶ֨קַח בֶּן־רְמַלְיָ֤הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם לַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה עָלֶ֑יהָ וְלֹ֥א יָכֹ֖ל לְהִלָּחֵ֥ם עָלֶֽיהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was in [the] days of Ahaz son of Jotham son of Uzziah, king of Judah, went up Rezin king of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah king of Israel [to] Jerusalem for battle against it, and not he was able to fight against it.

en.L: And it was in the days of Ahaz son of Jotham son of Uzziah, king of Judah, [that] Rezin king of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah, king of Israel, went up [to] Jerusalem for battle against it, and he was not able to fight against it.
en.B: In the days of Ahaz son of Jotham, the son of Uzziah, king of Judah, Rezin king of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah, king of Israel, came up to Jerusalem to make war on it, but they were not able to take it.
en.R: Ahaz son of Jotham, the grandson of Uzziah, was king of Judah. While he ruled, King Rezin of Aram and King Pekah son of Remaliah, who ruled the northern kingdom of Israel, came to attack Jerusalem. But they could not capture it.

es.L: Y sucedió en los días de Acaz hijo de Jotam, hijo de Uzías, rey de Judá, [que] Rezín, rey de Aram, y Peka hijo de Remalías, rey de Israel, subieron [a] Jerusalén para la guerra contra ella, pero no pudo combatir contra ella.
es.B: En los días de Acaz hijo de Jotam, hijo de Uzías, rey de Judá, Rezín, rey de Aram, y Peka hijo de Remalías, rey de Israel, subieron a Jerusalén para hacerle la guerra, pero no pudieron tomarla.
es.R: Acaz hijo de Jotam, nieto de Uzías, era rey de Judá. Mientras él gobernaba, el rey Rezín de Aram y el rey Peka hijo de Remalías, que gobernaba el reino de Israel en el norte, vinieron a atacar Jerusalén. Pero no pudieron conquistarla.

fr.L: Et il arriva, aux jours d’Achaz fils de Jotham fils d’Ozias, roi de Juda, [que] Retsin, roi d’Aram, et Péqah fils de Remalia, roi d’Israël, montèrent [contre] Jérusalem pour lui faire la guerre, et il ne put pas la combattre.
fr.B: Au temps d’Achaz fils de Jotham, fils d’Ozias, roi de Juda, Retsin, roi d’Aram, et Péqah fils de Remalia, roi d’Israël, montèrent contre Jérusalem pour lui faire la guerre, mais ils ne purent pas la prendre.
fr.R: Achaz fils de Jotham, petit-fils d’Ozias, était roi de Juda. Pendant son règne, le roi Retsin d’Aram et le roi Péqah fils de Remalia, qui régnait sur le royaume du nord, Israël, sont venus attaquer Jérusalem. Mais ils n’ont pas réussi à la prendre.

sw.L: Ikawa katika siku za Ahazi mwana wa Yothamu mwana wa Uzia, mfalme wa Yuda, [kwamba] Resini mfalme wa Aramu na Peka mwana wa Remalia, mfalme wa Israeli, walipanda [kwenda] Yerusalemu kuupiga vita, wala hakuweza kuupiga.
sw.B: Katika siku za Ahazi mwana wa Yothamu, mwana wa Uzia, mfalme wa Yuda, Resini mfalme wa Aramu na Peka mwana wa Remalia, mfalme wa Israeli, walipanda kuja Yerusalemu kuushambulia, lakini hawakuweza kuuteka.
sw.R: Ahazi mwana wa Yothamu, mjukuu wa Uzia, alikuwa mfalme wa Yuda. Alipokuwa akitawala, mfalme Resini wa Aramu na mfalme Peka mwana wa Remalia, aliyetawala ufalme wa kaskazini wa Israeli, walikuja kuushambulia Yerusalemu. Lakini hawakuweza kuuteka.

vi.L: Xảy ra trong thời A-cha con trai Giô-tham, con trai Ô-xia, vua Giu-đa, Rê-xin vua A-ram và Phê-ca con trai Rê-ma-lia, vua Y-sơ-ra-ên, đi lên [đánh] Giê-ru-sa-lem để giao chiến với nó, nhưng không thể đánh thắng nó.
vi.B: Trong thời A-cha con trai Giô-tham, cháu Ô-xia, làm vua Giu-đa, Rê-xin vua A-ram và Phê-ca con trai Rê-ma-lia, vua Y-sơ-ra-ên, kéo lên đánh Giê-ru-sa-lem, nhưng không chiếm được thành.
vi.R: A-cha con trai Giô-tham, cháu của Ô-xia, làm vua Giu-đa. Trong thời vua cai trị, vua Rê-xin của A-ram và vua Phê-ca con trai Rê-ma-lia, người cai trị vương quốc Y-sơ-ra-ên ở phía bắc, kéo đến tấn công Giê-ru-sa-lem. Nhưng họ không chiếm được thành.

ko.L: 그리고 유다 왕 웃시야의 손자이며 요담의 아들인 아하스의 시대에, 아람 왕 르신과 이스라엘 왕 르말랴의 아들 베가가 예루살렘을 치려고 올라왔으나, 그가 그 성을 쳐서 [이길] 수 없었다.
ko.B: 웃시야의 손자이며 요담의 아들인 유다 왕 아하스가 다스리던 때에, 아람 왕 르신과 이스라엘 왕 르말랴의 아들 베가가 예루살렘을 치려고 올라왔으나, 그 성을 함락시키지 못했다.
ko.R: 요담의 아들이며 웃시야의 손자인 아하스가 유다의 왕이었다. 그가 다스리고 있을 때에 아람 왕 르신과 북쪽 이스라엘 나라를 다스리던 르말랴의 아들 베가 왕이 예루살렘을 공격하러 왔다. 그러나 그들은 그 성을 빼앗지 못했다.

decisions.choice: the attack of Rezin and Pekah on Jerusalem, told also in 2 Kings 16:5
decisions.reason: The opening of the verse matches 2 Kings 16:5 almost word for word. Rezin ruled Aram from Damascus, and Pekah ruled the northern kingdom of Israel from Samaria. The attack came in the 730s BC, while Assyria was pressing west; 2 Kings 16:7-9 and 2 Chronicles 28:5-21 tell how Ahaz answered it by sending for help to the king of Assyria.

decisions.choice: he was not able to fight against it: the attack failed to take the city
alternatives: they could not yet begin the attack on it
decisions.reason: The verse tells the outcome before the story of verses 2-9: the siege did not succeed. "Fight against it" here means to win the battle for it. The verb is singular in the Hebrew text, most likely with the two kings taken together or the leader of the attack in view; 2 Kings 16:5 and the Great Isaiah Scroll have the plural, "they were not able".

decisions.choice: they were not able to take it / they could not capture it
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "he was not able" refers to the attack of both kings, so Balanced and Readable say "they". Readable also says that Israel here is the northern kingdom, not Judah, and calls Uzziah Ahaz's grandson.

decisions.choice: Rezín, rey de Aram, y Peka hijo de Remalías, rey de Israel, subieron [a] Jerusalén para la guerra
decisions.reason: The opening matches 2 Kings 16:5, so the Spanish keeps the names and wording published there (subieron [a] Jerusalén para la guerra; no pudieron tomarla / conquistarla), changing only what the Hebrew of Isaiah changes.

decisions.choice: "Resini", "Peka mwana wa Remalia", "Aramu"
decisions.reason: The names keep their forms in 2 Kings 15-16, where the same attack is told (m1).

decisions.choice: "Retsin ... Péqah fils de Remalia"
decisions.reason: The verse is nearly the same Hebrew as 2 Kings 16:5, whose published French names and wording are reused; narration in the passé simple at Literal and Balanced, passé composé at Readable.

decisions.choice: "아하스", "르신", "르말랴의 아들 베가", as 2 Kings 16:5
alternatives: | The published Korean names of the same event (meaning decision m1).

source.text: וַיֻּגַּ֗ד לְבֵ֤ית דָּוִד֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר נָ֥חָֽה אֲרָ֖ם עַל־אֶפְרָ֑יִם וַיָּ֤נַע לְבָבוֹ֙ וּלְבַ֣ב עַמּ֔וֹ כְּנ֥וֹעַ עֲצֵי־יַ֖עַר מִפְּנֵי־רֽוּחַ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was told to [the] house of David, saying, has settled Aram on Ephraim. And shook his heart and [the] heart of his people, as shake [the] trees of [the] forest before a wind.

en.L: And it was told to the house of David, saying, "Aram has settled on Ephraim." And his heart shook, and the heart of his people, as the trees of the forest shake before a wind.
en.B: Word came to the house of David: "Aram has camped in Ephraim." Then the king's heart and the hearts of his people shook, like the trees of a forest swaying in the wind.
en.R: Then the royal family of David received this report: "The army of Aram is camped in Ephraim, the land of Israel." King Ahaz and his people were terrified. They shook like trees in a forest when the wind blows.

es.L: Y se le informó a la casa de David, diciendo: «Aram se ha asentado sobre Efraín». Y se estremeció su corazón y el corazón de su pueblo, como se estremecen los árboles del bosque ante el viento.
es.B: Llegó la noticia a la casa de David: «Aram ha acampado en Efraín». Entonces el corazón del rey y el de su pueblo temblaron, como los árboles del bosque cuando los sacude el viento.
es.R: Entonces la familia real de David recibió esta noticia: «El ejército de Aram ha acampado en Efraín, la tierra de Israel». El rey Acaz y su pueblo se llenaron de terror. Temblaban como los árboles de un bosque cuando sopla el viento.

fr.L: Et on annonça à la maison de David, disant : « Aram s’est posé sur Éphraïm. » Et son cœur trembla, ainsi que le cœur de son peuple, comme tremblent les arbres de la forêt devant le vent.
fr.B: On vint annoncer à la maison de David : « Aram a établi son camp en Éphraïm. » Alors le cœur du roi et le cœur de son peuple tremblèrent, comme les arbres de la forêt s’agitent sous le vent.
fr.R: Alors la famille royale de David a reçu cette nouvelle : « L’armée d’Aram campe en Éphraïm, le pays d’Israël. » Le roi Achaz et son peuple ont été pris de terreur. Ils tremblaient comme les arbres d’une forêt quand le vent souffle.

sw.L: Ikaambiwa nyumba ya Daudi, kusema, "Aramu amepiga kambi katika Efraimu." Na moyo wake ukatetemeka, na moyo wa watu wake, kama miti ya msituni inavyotetemeka mbele ya upepo.
sw.B: Habari zilifika kwa nyumba ya Daudi: "Aramu amepiga kambi katika Efraimu." Ndipo moyo wa mfalme na mioyo ya watu wake ikatetemeka, kama miti ya msituni inavyoyumbishwa na upepo.
sw.R: Kisha jamaa ya kifalme ya Daudi ilipata habari hii: "Jeshi la Aramu limepiga kambi katika Efraimu, nchi ya Israeli." Mfalme Ahazi na watu wake waliogopa sana. Walitetemeka kama miti ya msituni upepo unapovuma.

vi.L: Có người báo cho nhà Đa-vít rằng: "A-ram đã đóng lại trên Ép-ra-im." Lòng vua và lòng dân vua rung động như cây trong rừng rung động trước gió.
vi.B: Có tin báo đến nhà Đa-vít: "Quân A-ram đã đóng trại trong đất Ép-ra-im." Lòng vua và lòng dân chúng run sợ như cây rừng lay động trước gió.
vi.R: Bấy giờ hoàng tộc Đa-vít nhận được tin này: "Quân đội A-ram đang đóng trại tại Ép-ra-im, tức là đất Y-sơ-ra-ên." Vua A-cha và dân chúng hết sức kinh hãi. Họ run rẩy như cây cối trong rừng khi gió thổi.

ko.L: 그리고 다윗의 집에 "아람이 에브라임에 머물렀다" 하는 소식이 전해졌다. 그러자 그의 마음과 그의 백성의 마음이 숲의 나무들이 바람 앞에 흔들리듯 흔들렸다.
ko.B: "아람 군대가 에브라임에 진을 쳤다"는 소식이 다윗 왕실에 전해졌다. 그러자 왕의 마음과 백성의 마음이 바람에 흔들리는 숲의 나무들처럼 떨렸다.
ko.R: 그때 다윗의 왕실에 이런 소식이 들어왔다. "아람 군대가 이스라엘 땅 에브라임에 진을 치고 있다." 아하스 왕과 그의 백성은 몹시 두려워했다. 그들은 바람이 불 때 숲의 나무들이 흔들리듯 떨었다.

decisions.choice: Aram has settled on Ephraim: the army of Aram has come to rest in Ephraim's land
decisions.reason: The verb means to come to rest or settle, as the locusts "settled" on Egypt (Exodus 10:14). Here it most likely means that Aram's troops are camped in Ephraim, close to Judah's border. It may instead mean that Aram has joined with Ephraim as an ally; either way the two are acting together against Judah.

decisions.choice: Ephraim: the northern kingdom of Israel
decisions.reason: Ephraim was the leading tribe of the northern kingdom, and Isaiah often uses its name for that whole kingdom (verses 5, 8, 9, 17).

decisions.choice: the house of David ... his heart: the royal house, with Ahaz at its head
decisions.reason: "The house of David" is the reigning family of David's line, to whom God promised a lasting throne (2 Samuel 7:16). "His heart" is the king's, Ahaz's. The shaking trees picture the panic of king and people alike.

decisions.choice: the king's heart / King Ahaz
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "his heart"; Balanced and Readable say whose. Readable also says "the army of Aram" and explains that Ephraim is the land of Israel, and it says "terrified" for the shaking heart.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָה֮ אֶֽל־יְשַׁעְיָהוּ֒ צֵא־נָא֙ לִקְרַ֣את אָחָ֔ז אַתָּ֕ה וּשְׁאָ֖ר יָשׁ֣וּב בְּנֶ֑ךָ אֶל־קְצֵ֗ה תְּעָלַת֙ הַבְּרֵכָ֣ה הָעֶלְיוֹנָ֔ה אֶל־מְסִלַּ֖ת שְׂדֵ֥ה כוֹבֵֽס׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Yahweh to Isaiah, go out please to meet Ahaz, you and Shear-jashub your son, to [the] end of [the] conduit of the pool the upper, to [the] highway of [the] field of [the] washer,

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Isaiah, "Go out, please, to meet Ahaz, you and Shear-jashub your son, to the end of the conduit of the upper pool, on the highway to the Fuller's Field,
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Isaiah, "Take your son Shear-jashub and go out to meet Ahaz at the end of the water channel from the Upper Pool, on the road to the Fuller's Field,
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Isaiah, "Take your son Shear-jashub with you. (His name means 'A remnant will return.') Go out and meet Ahaz at the end of the water channel that comes from the Upper Pool. It is on the road to the field where cloth is washed.

es.L: Y dijo {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} a Isaías: «Sal ahora al encuentro de Acaz, tú y Sear-jasub tu hijo, al extremo del acueducto del estanque de arriba, en el camino del campo del Lavador,
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dijo a Isaías: «Toma a tu hijo Sear-jasub y sal al encuentro de Acaz en el extremo del canal del estanque de arriba, en el camino del campo del Lavador,
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dijo a Isaías: «Lleva contigo a tu hijo Sear-jasub. (Su nombre significa “Un remanente volverá”). Sal a encontrarte con Acaz en el extremo del canal que viene del estanque de arriba. Está en el camino del campo donde se lava la ropa.

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit à Isaïe : « Sors donc à la rencontre d’Achaz, toi et Shear-Yashouv ton fils, au bout de l’aqueduc du réservoir supérieur, sur la route du champ du Foulon,
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit à Isaïe : « Prends ton fils Shear-Yashouv et sors à la rencontre d’Achaz, au bout du canal du réservoir supérieur, sur la route du champ du Foulon,
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a dit à Isaïe : « Emmène avec toi ton fils Shear-Yashouv. (Son nom veut dire “Un reste reviendra”.) Va à la rencontre d’Achaz au bout du canal qui vient du réservoir supérieur. Il se trouve sur la route du champ où l’on lave les étoffes.

sw.L: Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia Isaya, "Toka, tafadhali, uende kukutana na Ahazi, wewe na Shear-yashubu mwanao, kwenye mwisho wa mfereji wa bwawa la juu, katika njia kuu ya shamba la dobi,
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimwambia Isaya, "Mchukue mwanao Shear-yashubu, mtoke mkakutane na Ahazi kwenye mwisho wa mfereji wa maji wa Bwawa la Juu, katika njia iendayo Shamba la Dobi,
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimwambia Isaya, "Mchukue mwanao Shear-yashubu pamoja nawe. (Jina lake linamaanisha 'Mabaki watarudi.') Nendeni mkakutane na Ahazi kwenye mwisho wa mfereji wa maji unaotoka Bwawa la Juu. Uko katika njia iendayo kwenye shamba wanakofulia nguo.

vi.L: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với Ê-sai: "Hãy đi ra gặp A-cha, ngươi và Sê-a Gia-súp con trai ngươi, tại cuối cống dẫn nước của hồ trên, trên đường cái đến Cánh Đồng Thợ Giặt,
vi.B: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với Ê-sai: "Con hãy dẫn Sê-a Gia-súp, con trai con, đi ra gặp A-cha ở cuối cống dẫn nước của Hồ Trên, bên đường đến Cánh Đồng Thợ Giặt,
vi.R: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với Ê-sai: "Con hãy dẫn Sê-a Gia-súp, con trai con, đi cùng. (Tên ấy có nghĩa là 'Một số người còn sót lại sẽ trở về.') Hãy đi ra gặp A-cha ở cuối cống dẫn nước từ Hồ Trên. Chỗ ấy ở bên đường đến cánh đồng nơi người ta giặt vải.

ko.L: 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이사야에게 말씀하셨다. "너는 네 아들 스알야숩과 함께 나가서, 세탁자의 밭으로 가는 큰길에 있는 윗못의 수로 끝에서 아하스를 만나라.
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이사야에게 말씀하셨다. "너는 네 아들 스알야숩을 데리고 나가서, 세탁자의 밭으로 가는 길에 있는 윗못의 수로 끝에서 아하스를 만나라.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이사야에게 말씀하셨다. "네 아들 스알야숩을 데리고 가거라. (그 이름은 '남은 사람들이 돌아올 것이다'라는 뜻이다.) 가서 윗못에서 흘러나오는 수로 끝에서 아하스를 만나라. 그곳은 천을 빨아 말리는 밭으로 가는 길가에 있다.

decisions.choice: Shear-jashub: a name meaning "a remnant will return"
decisions.reason: Isaiah's son carries a message in his name, as Isaiah says of his children in 8:18. "A remnant will return" can be heard as a warning (only a remnant will survive) and as a hope (a remnant will come back, or turn back to God). Isaiah 10:20-22 uses the same words in both ways.

decisions.choice: the end of the conduit of the upper pool: the place where the Assyrian envoy later stands
decisions.reason: The same spot is named in 36:2 (and 2 Kings 18:17), where the king of Assyria's commander demands that Hezekiah surrender. Here, at the water channel that served the city, Ahaz is called to trust God; there, his son Hezekiah faces the very power Ahaz turned to.

decisions.choice: the washer's field: where cloth was washed and treated
decisions.reason: A fuller cleaned and thickened new woolen cloth with water, trampling and beating it. The work needed plenty of water, so it was done near a water supply outside the city wall.

decisions.choice: (His name means 'A remnant will return.') ... the field where cloth is washed
decisions.reason: Readable gives the meaning of Shear-jashub's name, which is part of the message, and explains the name of the field. Literal and Balanced keep the old name "the Fuller's Field".

decisions.choice: Sear-jasub ... el estanque de arriba ... el campo del Lavador
decisions.reason: The name follows the terms note; the place is the one named in 2 Kings 18:17, so the Spanish keeps the wording published there (acueducto / canal del estanque de arriba, el campo del Lavador; R el campo donde se lava la ropa).

decisions.choice: "Shear-yashubu"; R explains "Mabaki watarudi"
decisions.reason: The form set in the terms note; Readable gives the meaning of the name, as the English Readable does (m1), using "mabaki", the word for remnant.

decisions.choice: "Shear-Yashouv"
decisions.reason: The terms note’s form of the name, with "ou" for the Hebrew u and "sh" as in Shéol and Shiméï.

decisions.choice: "Sê-a Gia-súp", with the meaning given at R

decisions.choice: two tails of smoking firebrands: two kings whose fire is nearly out
decisions.reason: A firebrand is a stick pulled from the fire. Its "tail" is the burnt stub that is left, giving off smoke but little heat. The two kings look fierce, but their power is almost spent. Within a few years both were gone (verse 16; 2 Kings 15:30; 16:9).

decisions.choice: take care and be quiet: stay on guard, and keep calm in trust
decisions.reason: The first verb means to watch oneself, to be on guard; the second to be still and undisturbed. Ahaz is not to act in panic. Isaiah later says the same to the people: "In quietness and in trust shall be your strength" (30:15).

decisions.choice: the son of Remaliah: Pekah, named only by his father's name
decisions.reason: Isaiah never names Pekah in this chapter (verses 4, 5, 9). Calling a king only "son of" someone may show scorn, as Saul spoke of David as "the son of Jesse" (1 Samuel 20:27-31).

decisions.choice: Pekah ... They are angry, but they are like two burned-out sticks ... Their fire is almost out.
decisions.reason: Readable names Pekah and explains the picture of the smoking stubs in plain words. Literal and Balanced keep the image as it stands.

decisions.choice: the prophet's message to Ahaz says "vua"
decisions.reason: Isaiah carries the message and speaks to the king as Kings has the prophet do (terms note: the prophet calls the king "vua"); God's own "Ta" returns only where the oracle speaks in the first person.

decisions.choice: God's message to Ahaz in the plain style (해라체) inside God's words to Isaiah
alternatives: 합쇼체 for a message to a king
decisions.reason: God speaks in 해라체 to everyone, kings included; when Isaiah himself speaks to the king (verses 13-25) he uses 합쇼체, as in 2 Kings 20:1.

decisions.choice: let us terrify it: fill it with dread
decisions.reason: The verb most likely comes from a root meaning to dread or be in terror, here "make it dread". It may instead come from a root meaning to cut off or tear apart, "let us tear it apart". Either way it describes a fierce attack.

decisions.choice: let us break into it for ourselves: breach its walls and take it
decisions.reason: The verb means to split or break open, used of breaching a city's wall (2 Kings 25:4; 2 Chronicles 32:1). "For ourselves" means to take it over.

decisions.choice: the son of Tabeel: a man otherwise unknown, whom the two kings meant to put on David's throne
decisions.reason: Tabeel means "God is good" (compare Ezra 4:7). The vowels of the Hebrew text give a slightly different form that sounds like "good for nothing", perhaps a mocking twist of the name. Nothing else is known of him. The plan would have ended the line of David's kings, which God had promised to keep (2 Samuel 7:16).

decisions.choice: We will
decisions.reason: Readable says "We will" for the plotting kings' "Let us", which reads more easily.

decisions.choice: single quotation marks ‘ ’
decisions.reason: The kings’ words are quoted inside the message Isaiah is to give Ahaz, which is itself inside the LORD’s words, so French uses a third level of quotation marks.

decisions.choice: "Ta-bê-ên"
decisions.reason: A transliterated name; the "Ta" that begins it is part of the name and takes no deity_pronoun span.

decisions.choice: it will not stand, and it will not be: the plan will fail
decisions.reason: "Stand" means to hold good or come true. The plan of the two kings will not happen. In 8:10 Isaiah says the same of every plan made against God's people, and in 14:24 that what God plans will stand.

decisions.choice: the head of Aram is Damascus ... Rezin: these kingdoms have only human heads
decisions.reason: Verses 8-9 name the capital and the king of each attacker. The point seems to be that they are only what they are, a city and a man, and no more; Judah has the LORD's promise to the house of David. The verses leave this contrast unspoken.

decisions.choice: within sixty-five years Ephraim will be shattered: the end of the northern kingdom
decisions.reason: Samaria fell to Assyria in 722 BC, little more than a dozen years later, and its people were carried off (2 Kings 17:6). After that the kings of Assyria settled foreign peoples in the land, as late as the reign of Esarhaddon (2 Kings 17:24; Ezra 4:2), and Ephraim no longer existed as a people. Sixty-five years from Ahaz's time reaches into that later period. The sentence breaks the pattern of the paired lines in verses 8-9.

decisions.choice: capital ... ruler
decisions.reason: "Head" is used in two senses: the chief city of a country and the king of a city. Readable says "capital" and "ruler"; Literal and Balanced keep "head" for both.

decisions.choice: believe ... be established: a play on one root, to be firm
decisions.reason: Both verbs come from the same root, meaning to be firm or sure. The first means to trust, to hold firm on someone; the second to be made firm, to last. The same verb is used in God's promise to David, "your house and your kingdom shall be made sure" (2 Samuel 7:16). The house of David will stand only if it trusts God.

decisions.choice: you: plural, the house of David
decisions.reason: Both verbs are plural. The warning is addressed not only to Ahaz but to the whole royal house (verses 2, 13).

decisions.choice: you will not be established: the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The Septuagint reads "neither will you understand" for the second verb. The Hebrew text, with its play on one root, is followed here.

decisions.choice: hold firm in trust ... be held firm / trust firmly ... stand firm
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable repeat "firm" to keep the play on one root. Readable supplies "in God", whom the trust is in (verse 11). Readable also names Pekah.

decisions.choice: creen ... afirmados (L); firmes en la fe ... firmes (B); confían firmemente ... firmes (R)
decisions.reason: The two verbs share one root meaning "firm". B and R repeat "firmes" to keep the play; L keeps "creer" and "ser afirmado". Both verbs are plural, spoken to the house of David, so they take plural_you spans.

decisions.choice: "simama imara katika imani ... kusimamishwa imara"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew plays on one root, to be firm (m1); Balanced and Readable repeat "imara" to keep the echo, as the English does. Literal keeps the two verbs.

decisions.choice: "croyez ... affermis" (L); "tenez ferme ... tenus fermes" (B); "fermement ... debout" (R)
decisions.reason: French repeats the idea of firmness to keep something of the play on one root (*ʾaman*), as the English does; "vous" is plural, the house of David (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: "vững tin ... đứng vững" (B); "vững lòng tin cậy ... đứng vững" (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew plays on one root, to be firm (meaning decision); Vietnamese "vững" carries the play in both halves at Balanced and Readable. The "you" is plural, the house of David, so it is "các ngươi" in God's word.

decisions.choice: "믿다 ... 굳게 서다"; Balanced "믿음에 굳게 서지 않으면 ... 굳게 서지 못할 것이다"
decisions.reason: The two verbs share one root in Hebrew (meaning decision m1). Balanced repeats "굳게 서다" to carry the play; the archaic ending is avoided.

decisions.choice: a sign: something God does to confirm his word
decisions.reason: A sign is an event that shows a promise will come true, as the shadow on the steps did for Hezekiah (38:7-8) and the fleece did for Gideon (Judges 6:36-40). God offers Ahaz a sign that the attack will fail, so that he can trust.

decisions.choice: make the request deep: the vowels of the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The Hebrew vowels read "make the request deep". The same letters can be read "make it deep, to Sheol", the world of the dead, which gives a closer pair with "high above"; the Septuagint has "into the depth". The meaning is the same either way: any sign at all, from the lowest depths to the heights.

decisions.choice: deep ... high: from the depths to the heights, anything at all
decisions.reason: Naming the two extremes takes in everything between. Ahaz may ask for any sign he chooses.

decisions.choice: You may ask for anything, from deep under the earth to high in the sky.
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the two extremes.

decisions.choice: "dấu lạ" (sign)
decisions.reason: The word of the style guide for a sign that confirms God's word; the message comes through Isaiah, who calls the king "vua".

vi.R: Bấy giờ Ê-sai nói: "Hỡi dòng họ Đa-vít, hãy nghe đây! Các người làm cho người ta chán ngán các người. Như vậy chưa đủ sao? Nay các người còn làm cho Đức Chúa Trời của tôi cũng chán ngán các người nữa!

decisions.choice: he said ... my God: Isaiah speaks
decisions.reason: The speaker is Isaiah, who speaks for God. In verse 11 God was "your God" to Ahaz; now Isaiah says "my God". By refusing the sign, Ahaz has set himself apart from the God who offered it.

decisions.choice: house of David ... you: the royal house, addressed in the plural
decisions.reason: From here to verse 14 "you" is plural. Isaiah speaks to Ahaz as the head of David's royal line, the house to which God made his promise (2 Samuel 7:16).

decisions.choice: Isaiah
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "he said"; Balanced and Readable name Isaiah.

decisions.choice: Isaiah speaks to the royal house in the formal style (합쇼체) with "여러분", through verse 25
decisions.reason: The terms note: a prophet speaks to a king in 합쇼체 (2 Kings 20:1). The plural "you" is the house of David (meaning decision m2).

records.literal_gloss: Therefore will give [the] Lord he to you a sign: look, the young woman [is] pregnant and bearing a son, and she will call his name Immanuel.

en.L: Therefore the Lord {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} will give you a sign: look, the young woman [is] pregnant and bearing a son, and she will call his name Immanuel.
en.B: Because of this, the Lord {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} will give all of you a sign: see, the young woman is pregnant; she will give birth to a son and call him by the name Immanuel.
en.R: So the Lord {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} will give you a sign. A young woman is going to have a baby. She will give birth to a son and name him Immanuel, which means 'God is with us.'

es.L: Por tanto, el Señor mismo {{plural_you:les|os}} dará una señal: he aquí, la joven [está] encinta y da a luz un hijo, y le pondrá por nombre Emanuel.
es.B: Por eso, el Señor mismo {{plural_you:les dará a todos ustedes|os dará a todos vosotros}} una señal: la joven está embarazada; dará a luz un hijo y le pondrá por nombre Emanuel.
es.R: Así que el Señor mismo {{plural_you:les|os}} dará una señal. Una joven va a tener un bebé. Dará a luz un hijo y le pondrá por nombre Emanuel, que significa “Dios está con nosotros”.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi le Seigneur {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} vous donnera un signe : voici, la jeune femme [est] enceinte et enfante un fils, et elle l’appellera du nom d’Emmanuel.
fr.B: C’est pourquoi le Seigneur {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} vous donnera un signe : voici, la jeune femme est enceinte ; elle donnera naissance à un fils et elle l’appellera Emmanuel.
fr.R: Alors le Seigneur {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} vous donnera un signe. Une jeune femme va avoir un enfant. Elle donnera naissance à un fils et elle l’appellera Emmanuel, ce qui veut dire “Dieu est avec nous”.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo Bwana {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} atawapa ishara: tazama, msichana [ana] mimba na atamzaa mwana, naye atamwita jina lake Imanueli.
sw.B: Kwa sababu hiyo, Bwana {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} atawapa ninyi nyote ishara: angalieni, msichana ni mjamzito; atazaa mtoto wa kiume na kumpa jina Imanueli.

vi.L: Vì vậy chính Chúa sẽ ban cho các người một dấu lạ: kìa, người thiếu nữ đang mang thai, sẽ sinh một con trai và đặt tên là Em-ma-nu-ên.
vi.B: Vì thế, chính Chúa sẽ ban cho các người một dấu lạ: này, người thiếu nữ đang có thai; nàng sẽ sinh một con trai và đặt tên con là Em-ma-nu-ên.
vi.R: Vậy chính Chúa sẽ ban cho các người một dấu lạ. Một thiếu nữ sắp sinh con. Nàng sẽ sinh một con trai và đặt tên con là Em-ma-nu-ên, nghĩa là 'Đức Chúa Trời ở cùng chúng ta.'

ko.L: 그러므로 주님께서 친히 여러분에게 표징을 주실 것입니다. 보십시오, 그 젊은 여자가 임신하여 아들을 낳을 것이고, 그의 이름을 임마누엘이라고 부를 것입니다.
ko.B: 그러므로 주님께서 친히 여러분 모두에게 표징을 주실 것입니다. 보십시오, 그 젊은 여자가 임신하여 아들을 낳고, 그 이름을 임마누엘이라고 지을 것입니다.
ko.R: 그러니 주님께서 친히 여러분에게 표징을 주실 것입니다. 한 젊은 여자가 아기를 가질 것입니다. 그 여자가 아들을 낳아 그 이름을 임마누엘이라고 지을 것입니다. 그것은 "하나님께서 우리와 함께 계신다"라는 뜻입니다.

decisions.choice: the young woman: a girl or young woman of age to marry
decisions.reason: The word names a young woman who has come of age. It is used of Rebekah before her marriage (Genesis 24:43), who is also called a virgin (24:16); of Moses' sister as a girl (Exodus 2:8); of the young women in the royal court (Song of Songs 6:8); and in "the way of a man with a young woman" (Proverbs 30:19). It does not by itself say whether she is a virgin or married, though it is never clearly used of a married woman. The Septuagint, translated before the time of Jesus, rendered it with a word that usually means "virgin", and Matthew 1:23 quotes that form, seeing the sign fulfilled when Mary, a virgin, gave birth to Jesus. The article "the" may point to a woman Isaiah and the king both knew, or may simply mark her as the one in the sign.

decisions.choice: is pregnant and bearing a son: the time is open
alternatives: will conceive and bear a son
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has no verb "to be" here, so it can mean that she is already pregnant or that she will become pregnant; the Septuagint and Matthew 1:23 read it as future. "She will call" may also be read "you will call"; the Septuagint has "you" and Matthew has "they will call", and the Great Isaiah Scroll has a form that can mean "he will call" or "one will call". In Israel either parent could name a child (Genesis 4:25; 5:29).

decisions.choice: Immanuel: "God with us"
decisions.reason: The name means "God [is] with us", as Matthew 1:23 explains it. It answers the fear of verse 2: God is with his people. The sign belongs to Ahaz's day, for before the child is old enough to choose good and evil, the two kings' land will be deserted (verse 16). It also reaches further: the name returns in 8:8 and 8:10, a child born to rule on David's throne is promised in 9:5-6, and Matthew 1:22-23 says the birth of Jesus fulfilled this word.

decisions.choice: A young woman ... which means 'God is with us'
decisions.reason: Readable says "a young woman", since the reader is not told who she is; Literal and Balanced keep the Hebrew "the". Readable also gives the meaning of the name. Balanced says "all of you" because "you" is plural, the house of David.

decisions.choice: la joven (L, B); una joven (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word names a young woman of age to marry (meaning decision m1), so Spanish says "la joven" at L and B and "una joven" at R, never "la virgen". Matthew 1:23 has "la virgen", quoting the Greek of the Septuagint; the meaning decision and its footnote set out the question, and the rendering here follows the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: les / os ... (plural)
decisions.reason: From verse 13 the "you" is plural, the whole house of David (meaning decision m2 of verse 13), so the sign is given to "ustedes / vosotros", as the terms note sets it.

decisions.choice: "msichana" for *ʿalmah*
decisions.reason: "Msichana" is a girl or young woman of age to marry, the range of the Hebrew word (m1). "Mwanamwali" leans toward "virgin", and Matthew 1:23 has "bikira" from the Greek Septuagint's word; the English meaning decision and its footnote set out the question, so Swahili follows it and does not decide it.

decisions.choice: "Imanueli, maana yake 'Mungu yuko pamoja nasi'"
decisions.reason: The name keeps its form in Matthew 1:23; Readable gives its meaning, as the terms note settles.

decisions.choice: "la jeune femme" (L, B); "une jeune femme" (R)
decisions.reason: French follows the English meaning decision on the Hebrew word (*ʿalmah*); Matthew 1:23 quotes the Greek and the published French there says "la vierge", which the meaning decision’s footnote cites. Readable adds the meaning of the name, as Matthew 1:23 R.

decisions.choice: "vous"
decisions.reason: "You" is plural here, the house of David (verse 13), so French says "vous".

decisions.choice: "người thiếu nữ" (L, B); "một thiếu nữ" (R)
decisions.reason: The terms note's form: "thiếu nữ" is a young woman of age to marry, as the meaning decision reads the Hebrew word, and the published word for it in Proverbs 30:19. Matthew 1:23 has "trinh nữ" because it quotes the Greek, which says "virgin"; the meaning decision sets out both.

decisions.choice: "Em-ma-nu-ên"; at R with "nghĩa là 'Đức Chúa Trời ở cùng chúng ta'"
alternatives: "Đức Chúa Trời ở với chúng ta"
decisions.reason: The published name and meaning of Matthew 1:23, so a reader sees the quotation. "Chính Chúa" carries "the Lord himself" without a free pronoun, so no deity_pronoun span is needed.

decisions.choice: "그 젊은 여자" (L, B); "한 젊은 여자" (R), with "임신하여"
decisions.reason: The terms note: "처녀" is kept for *betulah* (2 Kings 19:21) and for the Greek of Matthew 1:23, which the English footnote cites; the Hebrew word here means a young woman of age to marry (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: "주님께서 친히"; "임마누엘", with Readable adding "'하나님께서 우리와 함께 계신다'라는 뜻입니다"
alternatives: | The terms note's forms (Matthew 1:23). Korean has no deity_pronoun span; "친히" carries "himself".

en.L: Curds and honey he will eat, at his knowing to reject the evil and choose the good.
en.B: Curds and honey will be his food by the time he can turn away from what is bad and choose what is good.
en.R: By the time he is old enough to know right from wrong, he will be eating curds and honey.

es.B: Cuajada y miel serán su alimento cuando ya sepa apartarse de lo malo y escoger lo bueno.
es.R: Para cuando tenga edad para distinguir entre el bien y el mal, estará comiendo cuajada y miel.

fr.B: Il se nourrira de crème et de miel jusqu’au jour où il saura se détourner du mal et choisir le bien.
fr.R: Quand il sera assez grand pour savoir ce qui est bien et ce qui est mal, il mangera de la crème et du miel.

sw.L: Atakula siagi na asali, wakati atakapojua kukataa ubaya na kuchagua wema.
sw.B: Maziwa ya mgando na asali vitakuwa chakula chake wakati atakapoweza kuacha lililo baya na kuchagua lililo jema.
sw.R: Wakati atakapokuwa na umri wa kutosha kutofautisha mema na mabaya, atakuwa akila maziwa ya mgando na asali.

vi.B: Sữa đông và mật ong sẽ là thức ăn của đứa trẻ cho đến lúc nó biết từ bỏ điều xấu và chọn điều tốt.
vi.R: Khi đứa trẻ đủ lớn để biết phân biệt đúng sai, nó sẽ ăn sữa đông và mật ong.

ko.L: 그가 악을 버리고 선을 택할 줄 알게 될 때에 엉긴 젖과 꿀을 먹을 것입니다.
ko.B: 그 아이가 나쁜 것을 버리고 좋은 것을 고를 줄 알게 될 무렵이면, 엉긴 젖과 꿀을 먹게 될 것입니다.
ko.R: 그 아이가 옳고 그른 것을 가릴 만큼 자랄 무렵에는 엉긴 젖과 꿀을 먹고 있을 것입니다.

decisions.choice: curds and honey: the food of a land that has gone back to pasture
alternatives: rich food, a sign of plenty
decisions.reason: Curds are thickened milk. Verses 21-22 explain them here: with fields left unworked, the few people who remain live on milk from their animals and honey from wild bees, not on grain and wine. Some read the food instead as a sign of plenty, like the "land flowing with milk and honey" (Exodus 3:8). In verses 21-22 it seems to be both: plenty for the few left in an emptied land.

decisions.choice: to reject the evil and choose the good: the age when a child can tell right from wrong
decisions.reason: The phrase marks the early years when a child begins to know good from bad (compare Deuteronomy 1:39). It sets a short time, a few years at most.

decisions.choice: by his knowing: by the time he knows
alternatives: so that he will know how to
decisions.reason: The preposition most likely marks time, "when he knows" or "by the time he knows". It can also mean purpose, "so that he will know".

decisions.choice: "siagi" (L), "maziwa ya mgando" (B, R) for curds
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is thickened milk (m1); Literal keeps the short word, and the other levels name the food Swahili readers know.

source.text: כִּ֠י בְּטֶ֨רֶם יֵדַ֥ע הַנַּ֛עַר מָאֹ֥ס בָּרָ֖ע וּבָחֹ֣ר בַּטּ֑וֹב תֵּעָזֵ֤ב הָאֲדָמָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אַתָּ֣ה קָ֔ץ מִפְּנֵ֖י שְׁנֵ֥י מְלָכֶֽיהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: For before knows the boy to reject in the evil and to choose in the good, will be forsaken the land which you [are] dreading from before [the] two of its kings.

en.L: For before the boy knows to reject the evil and choose the good, the land whose two kings you dread will be forsaken.
en.B: Even before the boy is able to turn from what is bad and choose what is good, the land of those two kings who frighten you will be abandoned.
en.R: Before the boy is old enough to know right from wrong, the lands of the two kings you are so afraid of will be empty.

es.L: Porque antes de que el niño sepa rechazar lo malo y escoger lo bueno, la tierra de cuyos dos reyes tienes pavor quedará abandonada.
es.B: Incluso antes de que el niño sea capaz de apartarse de lo malo y escoger lo bueno, la tierra de esos dos reyes que te asustan quedará abandonada.
es.R: Antes de que el niño tenga edad para distinguir entre el bien y el mal, los países de los dos reyes a los que tanto temes quedarán vacíos.

fr.L: Car avant que l’enfant sache rejeter le mal et choisir le bien, le pays dont tu redoutes les deux rois sera abandonné.
fr.B: Avant même que l’enfant soit capable de se détourner du mal et de choisir le bien, le pays des deux rois qui te font peur sera abandonné.
fr.R: Avant que l’enfant soit assez grand pour savoir ce qui est bien et ce qui est mal, les pays des deux rois qui te font si peur seront vides.

sw.L: Kwa maana kabla mvulana hajajua kukataa ubaya na kuchagua wema, nchi ambayo unawaogopa wafalme wake wawili itaachwa.
sw.B: Hata kabla mvulana hajaweza kuacha lililo baya na kuchagua lililo jema, nchi ya wafalme hao wawili wanaokutisha itaachwa ukiwa.
sw.R: Kabla mvulana huyo hajakua kiasi cha kutofautisha mema na mabaya, nchi za wale wafalme wawili mnaowaogopa sana zitakuwa tupu.

vi.L: Vì trước khi đứa trẻ biết bỏ điều ác và chọn điều lành, đất của hai vua mà vua đang khiếp sợ sẽ bị bỏ hoang.
vi.B: Ngay cả trước khi đứa trẻ biết từ bỏ điều xấu và chọn điều tốt, đất của hai vua mà vua đang sợ hãi sẽ bị bỏ hoang.
vi.R: Trước khi đứa trẻ đủ lớn để biết phân biệt đúng sai, đất đai của hai vua mà vua đang rất sợ sẽ trở nên hoang vắng.

ko.L: 그 아이가 악을 버리고 선을 택할 줄 알기 전에, 임금님께서 두려워하시는 두 왕의 땅이 버림받을 것이기 때문입니다.
ko.B: 그 아이가 나쁜 것을 버리고 좋은 것을 고를 줄 알기도 전에, 임금님을 떨게 하는 저 두 왕의 땅이 버려질 것입니다.
ko.R: 그 아이가 옳고 그른 것을 가릴 만큼 자라기 전에, 임금님께서 그토록 두려워하시는 두 왕의 나라들이 텅 비게 될 것입니다.

decisions.choice: the land of the two kings will be forsaken: Aram and Israel laid waste
decisions.reason: Within a few years Assyria took Damascus and killed Rezin (2 Kings 16:9, in 732 BC), and took Galilee and Gilead from Israel and carried their people away (2 Kings 15:29). Soon after, Pekah was murdered (2 Kings 15:30).

decisions.choice: the land whose two kings you dread: Aram and Israel taken together
decisions.reason: "The land" is singular, the territory of the two allied kings seen as one. "You" is now singular: Ahaz, who is in dread of them.

decisions.choice: the lands
decisions.reason: Readable says "lands" because two countries are meant.

decisions.choice: "임금님" for the singular "you", Ahaz
decisions.reason: Isaiah turns from the royal house to Ahaz himself; "임금님" with "-시-" is the respectful address to a king in this translation.

source.text: יָבִ֨יא יְהוָ֜ה עָלֶ֗יךָ וְעַֽל־עַמְּךָ֮ וְעַל־בֵּ֣ית אָבִיךָ֒ יָמִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹא־בָ֔אוּ לְמִיּ֥וֹם סוּר־אֶפְרַ֖יִם מֵעַ֣ל יְהוּדָ֑ה אֵ֖ת מֶ֥לֶךְ אַשּֽׁוּר׃פ

records.literal_gloss: Will bring Yahweh on you and on your people and on [the] house of your father days which not have come from [the] day of [the] departing of Ephraim from with Judah, the king of Assyria.

en.L: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will bring upon you and upon your people and upon the house of your father days which have not come since the day Ephraim departed from Judah: the king of Assyria.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will bring days on you, on your people, and on your royal house that have not been seen since Ephraim split off from Judah: the king of Assyria!
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will bring hard times on you, your people, and your royal family. There have been no days like them since the northern tribes split away from Judah. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will bring the king of Assyria against you.

es.L: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} traerá sobre ti y sobre tu pueblo y sobre la casa de tu padre días que no han venido desde el día en que Efraín se apartó de Judá: el rey de Asiria.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} traerá sobre ti, sobre tu pueblo y sobre tu casa real días como no se han visto desde que Efraín se separó de Judá: ¡el rey de Asiria!
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} traerá tiempos difíciles sobre ti, sobre tu pueblo y sobre tu familia real. No ha habido días como esos desde que las tribus del norte se separaron de Judá. {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} traerá contra ti al rey de Asiria.

fr.L: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} fera venir sur toi, et sur ton peuple, et sur la maison de ton père, des jours tels qu’il n’en est pas venu depuis le jour où Éphraïm s’est séparé de Juda : le roi d’Assyrie.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} fera venir sur toi, sur ton peuple et sur ta maison royale des jours comme on n’en a pas vu depuis qu’Éphraïm s’est séparé de Juda : le roi d’Assyrie !
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} fera venir des temps difficiles sur toi, sur ton peuple et sur ta famille royale. Il n’y en a pas eu de pareils depuis que les tribus du nord se sont séparées de Juda. {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} fera venir le roi d’Assyrie contre toi.

sw.L: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ataleta juu yako na juu ya watu wako na juu ya nyumba ya baba yako siku ambazo hazijaja tangu siku ile Efraimu alipojitenga na Yuda: mfalme wa Ashuru.
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atakuletea wewe, watu wako na nyumba yako ya kifalme siku ambazo hazijaonekana tangu Efraimu alipojitenga na Yuda: mfalme wa Ashuru!
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ataleta nyakati ngumu juu yako, watu wako na jamaa yako ya kifalme. Hapajakuwa na siku kama hizo tangu makabila ya kaskazini yalipojitenga na Yuda. {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atamleta mfalme wa Ashuru dhidi yenu.

vi.L: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ đem đến trên vua, trên dân vua và trên nhà cha vua những ngày chưa từng có từ ngày Ép-ra-im lìa khỏi Giu-đa: [tức là] vua A-si-ri.
vi.B: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ đem đến cho vua, cho dân vua và cho hoàng tộc của vua những ngày chưa từng thấy kể từ khi Ép-ra-im tách khỏi Giu-đa: đó là vua A-si-ri!
vi.R: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ đem những ngày khốn khó đến trên vua, dân của vua và hoàng tộc của vua. Chưa từng có những ngày như thế kể từ khi các chi tộc phía bắc tách khỏi Giu-đa. {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ đem vua A-si-ri đến đánh vua.

ko.L: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 임금님과 임금님의 백성과 임금님의 아버지의 집에, 에브라임이 유다에게서 떠나간 날 이후로 오지 않았던 날들을 오게 하실 것입니다. 곧 앗시리아 왕입니다.
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 임금님과 임금님의 백성과 왕실에, 에브라임이 유다에서 갈라져 나간 뒤로 한 번도 겪어 보지 못한 날들을 보내실 것입니다. 바로 앗시리아 왕입니다!
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 임금님과 임금님의 백성과 왕실에 어려운 때를 보내실 것입니다. 북쪽 지파들이 유다에서 갈라져 나간 뒤로 그런 날은 없었습니다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 앗시리아 왕을 보내셔서 임금님을 치게 하실 것입니다.

decisions.choice: days which have not come: a time of disaster, which the king of Assyria will bring
alternatives: days of blessing such as have not been since the division
decisions.reason: The phrase alone could mean days of blessing, but the closing words, "the king of Assyria", show what kind of days they are: the power Ahaz looked to for help will become the threat (8:7-8). The Assyrian king of Ahaz's day was Tiglath-pileser III (2 Kings 16:7).

decisions.choice: since Ephraim departed from Judah: since the kingdom split
decisions.reason: After Solomon's death the northern tribes broke away from David's line and made Jeroboam their king (1 Kings 12:16-20), about two hundred years before Ahaz.

decisions.choice: the king of Assyria: added at the end to name the disaster
decisions.reason: The words stand at the end of the sentence, after the description of the days, and name what those days will bring.

decisions.choice: hard times ... will bring the king of Assyria against you
decisions.reason: Readable says what kind of days are meant and makes "the king of Assyria" a sentence of its own. It calls Ephraim "the northern tribes".

source.text: וְהָיָ֣ה׀בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא יִשְׁרֹ֤ק יְהוָה֙ לַזְּב֔וּב אֲשֶׁ֥ר בִּקְצֵ֖ה יְאֹרֵ֣י מִצְרָ֑יִם וְלַ֨דְּבוֹרָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּאֶ֥רֶץ אַשּֽׁוּר׃

records.literal_gloss: And it will be in the day the that, will whistle Yahweh for the fly which [is] at [the] end of [the] streams of Egypt and for the bee which [is] in [the] land of Assyria.

en.L: And it will be in that day, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will whistle for the fly that [is] at the end of the streams of Egypt and for the bee that [is] in the land of Assyria.
en.B: On that day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will whistle for the fly from the farthest streams of Egypt and for the bee in the land of Assyria.
en.R: At that time {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will whistle to call armies from Egypt and Assyria. They will come like flies from the far-off streams of Egypt and like bees from the land of Assyria.

es.L: Y sucederá en aquel día que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} silbará a la mosca que [está] en el extremo de los ríos de Egipto, y a la abeja que [está] en la tierra de Asiria.
es.B: Aquel día {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} llamará con un silbido a la mosca de los ríos más lejanos de Egipto y a la abeja de la tierra de Asiria.
es.R: En ese tiempo {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} silbará para llamar a ejércitos de Egipto y de Asiria. Vendrán como moscas desde los lejanos ríos de Egipto y como abejas desde la tierra de Asiria.

fr.L: Et il arrivera en ce jour-là que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} sifflera la mouche qui [est] au bout des fleuves de l’Égypte, et l’abeille qui [est] au pays d’Assyrie.
fr.B: Ce jour-là, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} sifflera la mouche des bras les plus lointains du Nil d’Égypte, et l’abeille du pays d’Assyrie.
fr.R: En ce temps-là, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} sifflera pour appeler des armées d’Égypte et d’Assyrie. Elles viendront comme des mouches des lointains bras du Nil, en Égypte, et comme des abeilles du pays d’Assyrie.

sw.L: Na itakuwa katika siku ile, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atampigia mluzi inzi aliye katika mwisho wa mito ya Misri, na nyuki aliye katika nchi ya Ashuru.
sw.B: Siku hiyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atampigia mluzi inzi kutoka mito ya mbali kabisa ya Misri, na nyuki kutoka nchi ya Ashuru.
sw.R: Wakati huo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atapiga mluzi kuyaita majeshi kutoka Misri na Ashuru. Yatakuja kama inzi kutoka mito ya mbali ya Misri na kama nyuki kutoka nchi ya Ashuru.

vi.L: Trong ngày ấy, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ huýt gọi ruồi ở tận cùng các sông ngòi Ai Cập và ong ở trong đất A-si-ri.
vi.B: Vào ngày ấy, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ huýt gọi ruồi từ những dòng sông xa nhất của Ai Cập và ong từ đất A-si-ri.
vi.R: Vào lúc ấy, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ huýt sáo gọi các đạo quân từ Ai Cập và A-si-ri. Họ sẽ kéo đến như ruồi từ những dòng sông xa xôi của Ai Cập, như ong từ đất A-si-ri.

ko.L: 그리고 그날에 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이집트 강들의 끝에 있는 파리와 앗시리아 땅에 있는 벌을 휘파람으로 부르실 것입니다.
ko.B: 그날에 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 휘파람을 불어 이집트의 먼 강들에서 파리 떼를 부르시고, 앗시리아 땅에서 벌 떼를 부르실 것입니다.
ko.R: 그때에 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 휘파람을 불어 이집트와 앗시리아의 군대를 부르실 것입니다. 그들은 이집트의 먼 강가에서 날아오는 파리 떼처럼, 앗시리아 땅에서 날아오는 벌 떼처럼 몰려올 것입니다.

decisions.choice: Yahweh will whistle: God calls the nations as easily as one calls an animal
decisions.reason: In 5:26 God whistles for a nation from the ends of the earth, and it comes quickly. The great powers come when God calls them.

decisions.choice: the fly ... the bee: armies swarming in
decisions.reason: Flies and bees stand for the armies of Egypt and Assyria, countless and stinging (compare Deuteronomy 1:44). The "streams of Egypt" are the channels of the Nile, and "the end" of them is the far south of Egypt.

decisions.choice: to call armies ... They will come like flies ... like bees
decisions.reason: Readable explains that the flies and bees are pictures of armies.

source.text: וּבָ֨אוּ וְנָח֤וּ כֻלָּם֙ בְּנַחֲלֵ֣י הַבַּתּ֔וֹת וּבִנְקִיקֵ֖י הַסְּלָעִ֑ים וּבְכֹל֙ הַנַּ֣עֲצוּצִ֔ים וּבְכֹ֖ל הַנַּהֲלֹלִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And they will come and they will settle, all of them, in [the] ravines of the steep places and in [the] clefts of the rocks and on all the thornbushes and on all the watering places.

en.L: And they will come and settle, all of them, in the ravines of the steep places and in the clefts of the rocks, and on all the thornbushes and on all the watering places.
en.B: They will all swarm in and settle in the gorges under the cliffs and in the cracks of the rocks, on every thorny shrub and at every place where the flocks drink.
en.R: All of them will come and settle everywhere: in deep valleys, in cracks in the rocks, on every thornbush, and at every place where animals drink.

es.L: Y vendrán y se posarán todas ellas en los barrancos de los despeñaderos y en las hendiduras de las rocas, y sobre todos los espinos y sobre todos los abrevaderos.
es.B: Todas llegarán en enjambre y se posarán en las quebradas bajo los acantilados y en las grietas de las rocas, en cada arbusto espinoso y en cada lugar donde beben los rebaños.
es.R: Todas vendrán y se posarán por todas partes: en los valles profundos, en las grietas de las rocas, en cada espino y en cada lugar donde beben los animales.

fr.L: Et elles viendront et se poseront, toutes, dans les ravins escarpés, et dans les fentes des rochers, et sur tous les buissons d’épines, et sur tous les abreuvoirs.
fr.B: Elles arriveront toutes en essaim et se poseront dans les gorges au pied des falaises et dans les fentes des rochers, sur chaque buisson épineux et à chaque point d’eau où boivent les troupeaux.
fr.R: Elles viendront toutes et se poseront partout : dans les vallées profondes, dans les fentes des rochers, sur chaque buisson d’épines et à chaque endroit où les animaux viennent boire.

sw.L: Nao watakuja na kutua, wote, katika mabonde ya magenge na katika nyufa za miamba, na juu ya michongoma yote na juu ya mahali pote pa kunyweshea.
sw.B: Wote watamiminika na kutua katika mabonde chini ya majabali na katika nyufa za miamba, juu ya kila kichaka cha miiba na kwenye kila mahali ambapo makundi ya wanyama hunywa maji.
sw.R: Wote watakuja na kutua kila mahali: katika mabonde marefu, katika nyufa za miamba, juu ya kila kichaka cha miiba, na kwenye kila mahali ambapo wanyama hunywa maji.

vi.L: Chúng sẽ đến và đậu lại, tất cả chúng, trong các khe núi dốc đứng, trong các kẽ đá, trên mọi bụi gai và trên mọi chỗ uống nước.
vi.B: Chúng sẽ kéo đến từng đàn và đậu xuống các hẻm núi dưới vách đá, trong các kẽ đá, trên mọi bụi gai và tại mọi nơi bầy súc vật uống nước.
vi.R: Tất cả chúng sẽ kéo đến và đậu khắp mọi nơi: trong các thung lũng sâu, trong các kẽ đá, trên mọi bụi gai và tại mọi chỗ súc vật uống nước.

ko.L: 그리고 그것들이 모두 와서 가파른 골짜기와 바위 틈과 모든 가시덤불과 모든 물 마시는 곳에 내려앉을 것입니다.
ko.B: 그것들이 모두 몰려와서 깎아지른 골짜기와 바위 틈과 가시덤불마다, 양 떼가 물 마시는 곳마다 내려앉을 것입니다.
ko.R: 그들은 모두 와서 깊은 골짜기와 바위 틈과 가시덤불마다, 짐승들이 물을 마시는 곳마다 내려앉을 것입니다.

decisions.choice: watering places: places where flocks drink
decisions.reason: The word is found only here, and its sense is uncertain. It most likely means a watering place for animals; it may instead mean a pasture.

decisions.choice: ravines, clefts, thornbushes, watering places: everywhere
decisions.reason: Like a swarm settling on every surface, the invaders will fill the land, from the wild places to the places where flocks are tended. There will be nowhere to hide (compare 2:19-21).

source.text: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֡וּא יְגַלַּ֣ח אֲדֹנָי֩ בְּתַ֨עַר הַשְּׂכִירָ֜ה בְּעֶבְרֵ֤י נָהָר֙ בְּמֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר אֶת־הָרֹ֖אשׁ וְשַׂ֣עַר הָרַגְלָ֑יִםוְגַ֥ם אֶת־הַזָּקָ֖ן תִּסְפֶּֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: In the day the that, will shave [the] Lord with a razor the hired in [the] regions beyond [the] River, with [the] king of Assyria, the head and [the] hair of the feet, and also the beard it will sweep away.

en.L: In that day the Lord will shave with the razor hired from beyond the River, with the king of Assyria, the head and the hair of the feet, and it will also sweep away the beard.
en.B: On that day the Lord will shave with a hired razor from beyond the Euphrates, the king of Assyria. He will shave the head and the hair of the body, and it will strip away the beard as well.
en.R: At that time the Lord will use the king of Assyria like a hired razor from beyond the Euphrates River. He will shave the heads and bodies of the people of Judah, and even their beards. It will be a terrible disgrace.

es.L: En aquel día el Señor afeitará con la navaja alquilada de más allá del Río, con el rey de Asiria, la cabeza y el vello de los pies, y también la barba arrancará.
es.B: Aquel día el Señor afeitará con una navaja alquilada de más allá del Éufrates, el rey de Asiria. Afeitará la cabeza y el vello del cuerpo, y también quitará la barba.
es.R: En ese tiempo el Señor usará al rey de Asiria como una navaja alquilada de más allá del río Éufrates. Afeitará la cabeza y el cuerpo de la gente de Judá, y hasta la barba. Será una vergüenza terrible.

fr.L: En ce jour-là, le Seigneur rasera avec le rasoir loué au-delà du Fleuve, avec le roi d’Assyrie, la tête et le poil des pieds, et il enlèvera aussi la barbe.
fr.B: Ce jour-là, le Seigneur rasera avec un rasoir loué au-delà de l’Euphrate, le roi d’Assyrie. Il rasera la tête et les poils du corps, et le rasoir enlèvera aussi la barbe.
fr.R: En ce temps-là, le Seigneur se servira du roi d’Assyrie comme d’un rasoir loué au-delà de l’Euphrate. Il rasera la tête et le corps des gens de Juda, et même leur barbe. Ce sera une terrible humiliation.

sw.L: Katika siku ile Bwana atanyoa kwa wembe ulioajiriwa ng'ambo ya Mto, kwa mfalme wa Ashuru, kichwa na nywele za miguu, nao utaondolea mbali ndevu pia.
sw.B: Siku hiyo Bwana atanyoa kwa wembe ulioajiriwa kutoka ng'ambo ya mto Frati, yaani, mfalme wa Ashuru. Atanyoa kichwa na nywele za mwili, nao utaziondoa ndevu pia.
sw.R: Wakati huo Bwana atamtumia mfalme wa Ashuru kama wembe ulioajiriwa kutoka ng'ambo ya mto Frati. Atanyoa vichwa na miili ya watu wa Yuda, na hata ndevu zao. Itakuwa aibu kubwa sana.

vi.L: Trong ngày ấy, Chúa sẽ dùng dao cạo thuê từ bên kia Sông, tức là vua A-si-ri, mà cạo đầu và lông chân, và nó cũng sẽ cạo sạch râu.
vi.B: Vào ngày ấy, Chúa sẽ dùng một con dao cạo thuê từ bên kia sông Ơ-phơ-rát, tức là vua A-si-ri, để cạo đầu và lông trên thân thể, và nó cũng sẽ cạo sạch cả râu.
vi.R: Vào lúc ấy, Chúa sẽ dùng vua A-si-ri như một con dao cạo thuê từ bên kia sông Ơ-phơ-rát. Ngài sẽ cạo đầu, cạo lông trên thân thể, và cạo luôn cả râu của dân Giu-đa. Đó sẽ là một sự nhục nhã ghê gớm.

ko.L: 그날에 주님께서 그 강 건너편에서 고용한 면도칼, 곧 앗시리아 왕으로 머리와 발의 털을 미실 것이고, 수염도 깎아 버리실 것입니다.
ko.B: 그날에 주님께서 유프라테스 강 건너편에서 빌려 온 면도칼, 곧 앗시리아 왕을 쓰셔서 머리털과 몸의 털을 미실 것이고, 수염까지 깎아 버리실 것입니다.
ko.R: 그때에 주님께서는 유프라테스 강 건너편에서 빌려 온 면도칼처럼 앗시리아 왕을 쓰실 것입니다. 주님께서 유다 백성의 머리와 몸의 털을 밀고 수염까지 깎으실 것입니다. 그것은 큰 수치가 될 것입니다.

decisions.choice: shaving the head and beard: shame and defeat
decisions.reason: To have one's beard shaved by another was a deep disgrace (2 Samuel 10:4-5), and captives might be shaved and stripped. The picture is of Judah humiliated and stripped bare by the invader.

decisions.choice: the hair of the feet: the hair of the body
alternatives: the hair of the private parts
decisions.reason: "Feet" here most likely means the legs and lower body, and it may be a polite way to speak of the private parts, as "feet" sometimes is (compare Judges 3:24). With the head and beard, it means the whole body is shaved.

decisions.choice: a hired razor from beyond the River: the king of Assyria
decisions.reason: "The River" is the Euphrates, which lay between Judah and Assyria. Ahaz paid the king of Assyria with silver and gold from the temple to come and help him (2 Kings 16:7-8); the one he hired will be the razor God uses against Judah.

decisions.choice: the Euphrates / the hair of the body / the people of Judah ... It will be a terrible disgrace.
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the Euphrates and say "body" for "feet". Readable says whose heads are shaved and states the shame the picture means.

decisions.choice: "Mto" (L), "mto Frati" (B, R) for the River
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "the River" with a capital, as Joshua 24:3 has "Ng'ambo ya Mto"; Balanced and Readable name it, as the English does, with the Swahili name "Frati".

decisions.choice: "bên kia Sông" (L); "bên kia sông Ơ-phơ-rát" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "the River" with a capital, as Joshua 24:2; Balanced and Readable name it, as the English does.

source.text: וְהָיָ֖ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא יְחַיֶּה־אִ֛ישׁ עֶגְלַ֥ת בָּקָ֖ר וּשְׁתֵּי־צֹֽאן׃

records.literal_gloss: And it will be in the day the that, will keep alive a man a heifer of [the] herd and two sheep.

en.L: And it will be in that day, a man will keep alive a heifer of the herd and two sheep.
en.B: On that day someone will keep a heifer and two sheep alive.
en.R: At that time a person will keep just one young cow and two sheep.

es.L: Y sucederá en aquel día que un hombre mantendrá viva una novilla de la vacada y dos ovejas.
es.B: Aquel día alguien criará una novilla y dos ovejas.
es.R: En ese tiempo una persona tendrá solo una vaca joven y dos ovejas.

fr.L: Et il arrivera en ce jour-là qu’un homme gardera en vie une génisse du troupeau et deux moutons.
fr.B: Ce jour-là, chacun gardera en vie une génisse et deux moutons.
fr.R: En ce temps-là, chaque famille ne gardera qu’une seule jeune vache et deux moutons.

sw.L: Na itakuwa katika siku ile, mtu atafuga mtamba mmoja wa ng'ombe na kondoo wawili.
sw.B: Siku hiyo mtu atawaweka hai mtamba mmoja na kondoo wawili.
sw.R: Wakati huo mtu atafuga ng'ombe mmoja mchanga tu na kondoo wawili.

vi.L: Trong ngày ấy, một người sẽ nuôi sống một con bò cái tơ trong bầy và hai con chiên.
vi.B: Vào ngày ấy, mỗi người sẽ nuôi được một con bò cái tơ và hai con chiên.
vi.R: Vào lúc ấy, mỗi người sẽ chỉ nuôi được một con bò cái tơ và hai con chiên.

ko.L: 그리고 그날에 사람이 어린 암소 한 마리와 양 두 마리를 기를 것입니다.
ko.B: 그날에 사람들은 어린 암소 한 마리와 양 두 마리만 살려 둘 것입니다.
ko.R: 그때에 사람들은 겨우 어린 암소 한 마리와 양 두 마리만 키울 것입니다.

decisions.choice: will keep alive a heifer and two sheep: a household reduced to a few animals
decisions.reason: After the invasion a family will have only a young cow and a couple of sheep or goats left. The next verse shows the other side: with so few people, these animals will have pasture enough to give plenty of milk.

decisions.choice: sheep: animals of the flock
decisions.reason: The word means animals of the flock, sheep or goats.

decisions.choice: just one
decisions.reason: Readable says "just one" to show how little is left, as the context implies.

source.text: וְהָיָ֗ה מֵרֹ֛ב עֲשׂ֥וֹת חָלָ֖ב יֹאכַ֣ל חֶמְאָ֑ה כִּֽי־חֶמְאָ֤ה וּדְבַשׁ֙ יֹאכֵ֔ל כָּל־הַנּוֹתָ֖ר בְּקֶ֥רֶב הָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it will be, from [the] abundance of producing milk he will eat curds, for curds and honey will eat every one who is left in [the] midst of the land.

en.L: And it will be, from the abundance of producing milk he will eat curds, for curds and honey every one who is left in the midst of the land will eat.
en.B: They will give so much milk that he will have curds to eat; indeed, curds and honey will be the food of all who are left in the land.
en.R: They will give plenty of milk, so he will have curds to eat. All the people still left in the land will live on curds and honey.

es.L: Y sucederá que, por la abundancia de la leche que darán, comerá cuajada; porque cuajada y miel comerá todo el que quede en medio de la tierra.
es.B: Darán tanta leche que tendrá cuajada para comer; en verdad, cuajada y miel serán el alimento de todos los que queden en el país.
es.R: Darán mucha leche, así que tendrá cuajada para comer. Toda la gente que todavía quede en el país vivirá de cuajada y miel.

fr.L: Et il arrivera qu’à cause de l’abondance du lait qu’elles produiront, il mangera de la crème, car de la crème et du miel mangera tout homme qui sera resté au milieu du pays.
fr.B: Elles donneront tant de lait qu’il aura de la crème à manger ; oui, la crème et le miel seront la nourriture de tous ceux qui seront restés dans le pays.
fr.R: Elles donneront beaucoup de lait, et il aura de la crème à manger. Tous ceux qui seront encore dans le pays vivront de crème et de miel.

sw.L: Na itakuwa, kwa wingi wa maziwa watakayotoa atakula siagi, kwa maana siagi na asali atakula kila mmoja aliyebaki katikati ya nchi.
sw.B: Watatoa maziwa mengi kiasi kwamba atapata maziwa ya mgando ya kula; naam, maziwa ya mgando na asali vitakuwa chakula cha wote watakaobaki katika nchi.
sw.R: Watatoa maziwa mengi, kwa hiyo atapata maziwa ya mgando ya kula. Watu wote watakaobaki katika nchi wataishi kwa maziwa ya mgando na asali.

vi.L: Và vì sữa sinh ra dồi dào, người sẽ ăn sữa đông; vì mọi người còn sót lại giữa xứ sẽ ăn sữa đông và mật ong.
vi.B: Chúng cho nhiều sữa đến nỗi người ấy có sữa đông để ăn; thật vậy, sữa đông và mật ong sẽ là thức ăn của mọi người còn sót lại trong xứ.
vi.R: Chúng sẽ cho nhiều sữa, nên người ấy sẽ có sữa đông để ăn. Tất cả những ai còn sót lại trong xứ sẽ sống nhờ sữa đông và mật ong.

ko.L: 그리고 그것들이 젖을 많이 내므로 그가 엉긴 젖을 먹을 것이니, 그 땅 가운데 남은 사람은 모두 엉긴 젖과 꿀을 먹을 것입니다.
ko.B: 그것들이 젖을 많이 내어 엉긴 젖을 먹게 될 것입니다. 그 땅에 남은 사람들은 모두 엉긴 젖과 꿀을 먹고 살 것입니다.
ko.R: 그 짐승들이 젖을 넉넉히 내어 사람들은 엉긴 젖을 먹을 것입니다. 그 땅에 아직 남아 있는 사람들은 모두 엉긴 젖과 꿀을 먹고 살 것입니다.

decisions.choice: plenty of milk, curds and honey: the food of herders in an emptied land
decisions.reason: With so few people and so much unworked land, a few animals give more milk than a family needs. People will live on milk and wild honey instead of grain and wine. This explains the curds and honey of verse 15.

decisions.choice: every one who is left: those who survive
decisions.reason: Only a remnant will remain in the land, as the name of Isaiah's son had said (verse 3). They will have enough, but the land will no longer be farmed.

source.text: וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא יִֽהְיֶ֣ה כָל־מָק֗וֹם אֲשֶׁ֧ר יִֽהְיֶה־שָּׁ֛ם אֶ֥לֶף גֶּ֖פֶן בְּאֶ֣לֶף כָּ֑סֶף לַשָּׁמִ֥יר וְלַשַּׁ֖יִת יִֽהְיֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And it will be in the day the that, will be every place where there was there a thousand vines for a thousand [of] silver, for thorns and for briers it will be.

en.L: And it will be in that day, every place where there were a thousand vines, [worth] a thousand [pieces of] silver, will become thorns and briers.
en.B: On that day every vineyard of a thousand vines, worth a thousand pieces of silver, will be overrun by thorns and briers.
en.R: At that time, every vineyard that had a thousand grapevines, worth a thousand pieces of silver, will be covered with thorns and briers.

es.L: Y sucederá en aquel día que todo lugar donde había mil vides, [que valían] mil [piezas de] plata, será para espinos y cardos.
es.B: Aquel día toda viña de mil vides, que valía mil piezas de plata, quedará invadida por espinos y cardos.
es.R: En ese tiempo toda viña que tenía mil vides, que valían mil monedas de plata, quedará cubierta de espinos y cardos.

fr.L: Et il arrivera en ce jour-là que tout lieu où il y avait mille ceps, [valant] mille [pièces d’]argent, deviendra ronces et épines.
fr.B: Ce jour-là, chaque vigne de mille ceps, qui valait mille pièces d’argent, sera envahie par les ronces et les épines.
fr.R: En ce temps-là, chaque vigne de mille ceps, qui valait mille pièces d’argent, sera couverte de ronces et d’épines.

sw.L: Na itakuwa katika siku ile, kila mahali palipokuwa na mizabibu elfu, [yenye thamani ya vipande] elfu vya fedha, patakuwa michongoma na miiba.
sw.B: Siku hiyo kila shamba la mizabibu elfu moja, lenye thamani ya vipande elfu vya fedha, litavamiwa na michongoma na miiba.
sw.R: Wakati huo kila shamba la mizabibu lililokuwa na mizabibu elfu moja, yenye thamani ya vipande elfu vya fedha, litafunikwa na michongoma na miiba.

vi.L: Trong ngày ấy, mọi nơi trước kia có một nghìn gốc nho, [trị giá] một nghìn [nén] bạc, sẽ thành gai góc và bụi gai.
vi.B: Vào ngày ấy, mọi vườn nho có một nghìn gốc nho, trị giá một nghìn miếng bạc, sẽ bị gai góc và bụi gai mọc tràn lan.
vi.R: Vào lúc ấy, mọi vườn nho có một nghìn gốc nho, trị giá một nghìn miếng bạc, sẽ bị gai góc và bụi gai phủ kín.

ko.L: 그리고 그날에 은 천 [개의 값어치가] 있는 포도나무 천 그루가 있던 곳마다 찔레와 가시덤불이 될 것입니다.
ko.B: 그날에는 은 천 개의 값어치가 있는 포도나무 천 그루가 자라던 곳마다 찔레와 가시덤불로 뒤덮일 것입니다.
ko.R: 그때에는 은 천 개만큼 값진 포도나무 천 그루가 자라던 포도밭마다 찔레와 가시덤불로 덮일 것입니다.

decisions.choice: a thousand vines for a thousand silver: the best vineyards
decisions.reason: A thousand vines worth a thousand pieces of silver, probably shekels, a silver coin for each vine, describes a large and valuable vineyard (compare Song of Songs 8:11). Even the richest land will go wild.

decisions.choice: thorns and briers: the vineyard left to ruin
decisions.reason: The same pair of words describes God's vineyard left unpruned and unhoed in 5:6, and they come back in 9:17, 10:17 and 27:4.

source.text: בַּחִצִּ֥ים וּבַקֶּ֖שֶׁת יָ֣בוֹא שָׁ֑מָּה כִּי־שָׁמִ֥יר וָשַׁ֖יִת תִּֽהְיֶ֥ה כָל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: With arrows and with bow one will come there, for thorns and briers will be all the land.

en.L: With arrows and with bow one will go there, for all the land will be thorns and briers.
en.B: Anyone who goes there will carry a bow and arrows, for thorns and briers will cover the whole land.
en.R: People will have to carry bows and arrows when they go there, because the whole land will be covered with thorns and briers.

es.L: Con flechas y con arco irá uno allí, porque toda la tierra será espinos y cardos.
es.B: Cualquiera que vaya allí llevará arco y flechas, porque los espinos y los cardos cubrirán todo el país.
es.R: La gente tendrá que llevar arcos y flechas cuando vaya allí, porque todo el país estará cubierto de espinos y cardos.

fr.L: Avec des flèches et avec l’arc on y ira, car tout le pays sera ronces et épines.
fr.B: Celui qui ira là portera un arc et des flèches, car les ronces et les épines couvriront tout le pays.
fr.R: Les gens devront emporter un arc et des flèches pour y aller, parce que tout le pays sera couvert de ronces et d’épines.

sw.L: Kwa mishale na kwa upinde mtu ataenda huko, kwa maana nchi yote itakuwa michongoma na miiba.
sw.B: Yeyote atakayekwenda huko atabeba upinde na mishale, kwa maana michongoma na miiba itaifunika nchi yote.
sw.R: Watu watalazimika kubeba pinde na mishale wanapokwenda huko, kwa sababu nchi yote itafunikwa na michongoma na miiba.

vi.L: Người ta sẽ mang tên và cung mà đến đó, vì cả xứ sẽ là gai góc và bụi gai.
vi.B: Ai đến đó đều phải mang theo cung tên, vì gai góc và bụi gai sẽ phủ khắp xứ.
vi.R: Người ta sẽ phải mang theo cung tên khi đến đó, vì cả xứ sẽ đầy gai góc và bụi gai.

ko.L: 사람들이 화살과 활을 가지고 그리로 갈 것입니다. 온 땅이 찔레와 가시덤불이 될 것이기 때문입니다.
ko.B: 그곳에 가는 사람은 누구나 활과 화살을 가지고 갈 것입니다. 온 땅이 찔레와 가시덤불로 뒤덮일 것이기 때문입니다.
ko.R: 사람들은 그곳에 갈 때 활과 화살을 가지고 가야 할 것입니다. 온 땅이 찔레와 가시덤불로 덮일 것이기 때문입니다.

decisions.choice: with arrows and bow: the land has become wild country
alternatives: people must go armed against wild animals
decisions.reason: Farmland will turn into wild, overgrown country, entered only by hunters or by people armed against wild animals. The verse does not say which; either way, no one will farm it.

source.text: וְכֹ֣ל הֶהָרִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר בַּמַּעְדֵּר֙ יֵעָ֣דֵר֔וּן לֹֽא־תָב֣וֹא שָׁ֔מָּה יִרְאַ֖ת שָׁמִ֣יר וָשָׁ֑יִת וְהָיָה֙ לְמִשְׁלַ֣ח שׁ֔וֹר וּלְמִרְמַ֖ס שֶֽׂה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And all the hills which with the hoe they were hoed, not you will go there [for] fear of thorns and briers; and it will be for a sending-out of ox and a trampling-place of sheep.

en.L: And all the hills which were hoed with the hoe, you will not go there [for] fear of thorns and briers; and it will be for a place where oxen are sent out and a trampling place of sheep."
en.B: As for the hills that used to be worked with the hoe, you will not go to them for fear of the thorns and briers. Oxen will be let out to graze there, and sheep will trample the ground."
en.R: People used to dig the soil on the hills with hoes. But no one will go there anymore, because they will be afraid of the thorns and briers. Cattle and sheep will be let loose there to graze and trample the ground."

es.L: Y a todos los montes que se cavaban con la azada, no irás allá por temor de los espinos y los cardos; y serán para soltar los bueyes y lugar pisoteado por las ovejas».
es.B: En cuanto a las colinas que antes se trabajaban con la azada, no irás a ellas por miedo a los espinos y los cardos. Allí soltarán los bueyes a pastar, y las ovejas pisotearán la tierra».
es.R: Antes la gente cavaba la tierra de las colinas con azadas. Pero ya nadie irá allí, porque tendrán miedo de los espinos y los cardos. Soltarán allí el ganado y las ovejas para que pasten y pisoteen la tierra».

fr.L: Et toutes les collines qu’on bêchait à la houe, tu n’y iras pas par crainte des ronces et des épines ; et elles serviront de lieu où l’on lâche le bœuf et où le mouton piétine. »
fr.B: Quant aux collines qu’on travaillait à la houe, tu n’y iras plus, par crainte des ronces et des épines. On y lâchera les bœufs pour paître, et les moutons piétineront le sol. »
fr.R: Autrefois, on retournait la terre des collines avec des houes. Mais plus personne n’y ira, parce qu’on aura peur des ronces et des épines. On y lâchera les bœufs et les moutons pour qu’ils broutent et piétinent le sol. »

sw.L: Na vilima vyote vilivyolimwa kwa jembe, hutakwenda huko kwa [kuogopa] michongoma na miiba; navyo vitakuwa mahali pa kuwaachia ng'ombe na pa kukanyagwa na kondoo."
sw.B: Na vile vilima vilivyokuwa vikilimwa kwa jembe, hamtakwenda huko kwa kuogopa michongoma na miiba. Ng'ombe wataachiwa kulisha huko, na kondoo watakanyaga ardhi."
sw.R: Watu walikuwa wakilima udongo wa vilimani kwa majembe. Lakini hakuna atakayekwenda huko tena, kwa sababu wataogopa michongoma na miiba. Ng'ombe na kondoo wataachiwa huko kula majani na kukanyaga ardhi."

vi.L: Còn mọi ngọn đồi trước kia được cuốc xới bằng cuốc, các người sẽ không đến đó [vì] sợ gai góc và bụi gai; nó sẽ thành nơi thả bò và chỗ chiên giày đạp."
vi.B: Còn những ngọn đồi trước kia được cuốc xới, các người sẽ không dám đến vì sợ gai góc và bụi gai. Bò sẽ được thả ra ăn cỏ ở đó, và chiên sẽ giẫm đạp mặt đất."
vi.R: Trước kia người ta dùng cuốc để xới đất trên các ngọn đồi. Nhưng không ai còn đến đó nữa, vì họ sợ gai góc và bụi gai. Bò và chiên sẽ được thả ra đó để ăn cỏ và giẫm đạp mặt đất."

ko.L: 그리고 괭이로 일구던 모든 언덕에, 찔레와 가시덤불이 두려워서 여러분이 그리로 가지 못할 것입니다. 그곳은 소를 풀어 놓는 곳과 양이 밟는 곳이 될 것입니다."
ko.B: 괭이로 일구던 언덕들에도 찔레와 가시덤불이 무서워 여러분이 가지 못할 것입니다. 그곳에는 소를 풀어 놓아 풀을 뜯게 하고, 양들이 땅을 밟고 다닐 것입니다."
ko.R: 사람들은 언덕에서 괭이로 땅을 일구곤 했습니다. 그러나 이제는 아무도 그곳에 가지 않을 것입니다. 찔레와 가시덤불이 무섭기 때문입니다. 그곳에는 소와 양을 풀어 놓아 풀을 뜯고 땅을 밟게 할 것입니다."

decisions.choice: you will not go there for fear of thorns and briers
alternatives: the fear of thorns and briers will not come there
decisions.reason: The verb can be read "you will go" or "it will come". If the second, the sense is that "the fear of thorns and briers will not come there": the hills once worked with the hoe will stay clear of thorns but become pasture. The first reading fits the picture of verses 23-24, where thorns cover the land.

decisions.choice: a place where oxen are let loose and sheep trample: farmland turned to pasture
decisions.reason: The hills that were once dug and planted will be left to the animals. Isaiah's prophecy against Judah's vineyard ends in the same way (5:5-6).

decisions.choice: no one
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "you" here means anyone; Readable says "no one".
